name: Camera
plain: Asks to use the camera for photos, video, scanning or video calls.
meaning: Sees the room, the face and documents in front of the lens. Apps can capture without a shutter sound in some modes, so both OSes add on-screen indicators.

android.prompt_ui: While using the app, Only this time, Don't allow (Android 11+)
android.persistence: Until revoked or auto-reset; one-time ends with the visible activity
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Permissions > Camera; Quick Settings camera access toggle (Android 12)
android.store_policy: Play: no declaration, but data-safety disclosure and background-capture limits
android.note: Capturing via the camera Intent needs no permission because the system camera app takes the picture.

ios.persistence: Until revoked; the prompt is shown only once per install
ios.note: Green dot appears in the status bar while the camera is in use (iOS 14).

data.update: up to 30 to 60 fps for preview; stills on demand

fields.name: frame
fields.range: up to sensor size, often 12 to 48 MP

limits.headline: Can use your camera while the app is open, after you tap Allow
limits.user_action: You tap Take photo, Scan, or Start video call, then tap Allow
can: Show what the camera sees and take photos or video
Capture one photo through the system camera app, with no permission, on Android
cannot: Use the camera without a green dot (iPhone) or green chip (Android 12 and later)
Use it after you tap Don't Allow
See your photo library; that is a separate permission
limits.differs: Android 11 and later adds Only this time. iPhone has OK or Don't Allow. Both show a dot or chip when the camera is on.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app take photos and video, scan codes and join video calls.

marketing.name: Camera privacy
marketing.pitch: iOS shows a green dot whenever an app uses the camera, so you always know.

marketing.name: CameraX
marketing.pitch: A simple camera library that lets apps take photos and video on many devices.

story.for_you: A pop up asks 'Allow camera?' once. Then the app can see what the lens sees, and a dot or chip tells you the camera is on.
story.for_makers: Camera access powers many features: scanning, video calls, effects and photos. Makers ask only when needed, because a no stops the whole feature and people trust apps that explain why.

use_cases.example: You post a story and filters add dog ears to your face live.
An AR game places a monster on your sidewalk.
You deposit a check by taking a picture of it.
You join a video call and see friends.
You scan a barcode to compare prices or try on furniture in your room.
A face unlock or ID check compares your face with a document.
You scan a QR code to pay at a market stall.

risks: Can capture without a shutter sound
story.android_note: Android shows a green camera chip and offers a one time grant.
story.ios_note: iOS shows a green dot and a one time grant, and Always Allow does not exist for camera.

technical_bounds: Cannot capture while the app is in the background on either OS (Android 11+ blocks background camera)
iPad multitasking and Stage Manager can keep sessions alive
Cannot run in background on either platform

linkedin.how: Used to take profile photos and video posts, and for ID verification: LinkedIn Verified passport checks need the app camera, the phone's NFC reader and a live selfie (Persona flow). Camera access is also listed in the Exodus Android report. Photos or Videos appear on the Apple label.

history.change: Privacy indicators and Quick Settings camera toggle added
Green indicator dot added; Control Center shows apps that recently used it
